correctness.rationale: Strict convexity (1<p<infinity), positive weights and r>0 give unique KKT minimizer, with signed weighted soft-threshold tau determined by sum_i w_i (|x_i|−tau*w_i^(q−1))_+=r outside the ball. On each strict active-set/sign cell S the exact Jacobian is sign-conjugate of J_S=I−a_S*w_S^T/W_S, zero extension off S. Every nonempty S is realized by positive interior outputs with strict inactive margins; continuity and finite piecewise-affine segment integration prove Lip=max{1,max_S||J_S||}. For p≠2, assuming norm-one on full support and differentiating ||v+t a||_p at t=0 for all v in kernel w forces weights equal pairwise; for |S|>=3, v=(1,1,-2) then forces p=2, so the only extra non-Hilbert case is equally weighted n=2. The outer-product formula for J_{1,2} gives displayed exact planar ratio. Independent numerical analytic dual-norm witness checked across six exponents and four weight pairs (24 comparisons); a finite experiment does not establish global quantifiers.
residual_risks: Real finite n, 1<p<infinity, wi>0, r>0 only; no endpoint/nonlinear-norm generalization.
Linear norm example tests do not certify infinite-parameter theorem.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge for final all-weight theorem. The published unweighted cross-polytope proof already gives thresholding, active-set centering and nonexpansivity for w=1, while the published planar wedge theorem implies the exact planar rank-one formula; neither covers arbitrary positive nonuniform weight vectors and all-dimensional weighted active-face operator-norm maximum, or its complete weight-sensitive nonexpansivity classification. Duchi et al cover only Euclidean projection; Denkowska studies existence of contractive maps and linear subspaces, not the exact nearest-point Lipschitz modulus. The overlap of the unweighted and planar subclaims is explicitly conceded: acceptance is for the surviving unified anisotropic-weight all-dimension result, not for novelty of its known specializations.
residual_risks: A yet-uninspected general weighted metric-projection result in Banach-space approximation literature could cover more; indexed and directly relevant full sources checked do not establish such implication.
Finite norm maximum may require nonlinear numerical operator-norm optimization for larger support; no elementary expression claimed.
Known unweighted and planar specializations do not count toward novel contribution.
